topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing and outlines the intended learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor virology and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical discovery of oncogenes through tumor viruses and the laboratory assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional classification and mechanisms of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer-driving mutations are categorized and illustrate their mechanistic effects on key regulatory proteins such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how distinct defects in DNA repair, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Stepwise tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how inherited and acquired mutations accumulate to drive multistep cancer progression and malignant development.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks, recommended reading materials, and a preview of the next lecture.
